summary: Google's email service provides extensive API access via OAuth2, but apps requesting broad access to mail data (restricted scopes) must undergo rigorous security audits and paid assessments.

verdict.why: Requests for full Gmail access (restricted scopes) trigger a mandatory CASA Tier 2 security assessment, which costs up to $1,000 and requires several weeks of review.
verdict.approvalTrigger: Requesting restricted scopes (like mail.google.com) for an 'External' app status.

oauth.refreshTokens: Requires access_type=offline; tokens expire in 7 days while in Testing mode.
oauth.redirectUriRules: HTTPS mandatory for production; localhost allowed for dev; exact matching required; domain must be in 'Authorized Domains' list.
oauth.scopeNotes: Default Composio scopes include 'mail.google.com', which is a Restricted scope requiring CASA Tier 2 assessment.

prerequisites.detail: A project must be created in the Google Cloud Console.
Must manually enable the 'Gmail API' in the API Library.
Must include a 'Limited Use' disclosure statement specifically for Google API data.

steps.title: Enable Gmail API
steps.detail: Navigate to API Library in Google Cloud Console and enable 'Gmail API' for your project.

steps.title: Configure Consent Screen
steps.detail: Set up the OAuth consent screen with app name, support email, and developer contact info.

steps.title: Add Scopes and Test Users
steps.detail: Add the required Gmail scopes. While in 'Testing' mode, you must manually add up to 100 test user emails to allow them to connect.

steps.title: Generate Credentials
steps.detail: Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID for a 'Web application' and set the redirect URI.

steps.title: Develop Integration
steps.detail: Implement OAuth flow using client ID and secret, ensuring access_type=offline is used.

steps.title: Draft Verification Materials
steps.detail: Prepare the YouTube demo video showing the full OAuth flow and how the data is used in the app.

steps.title: Submit for App Verification
steps.detail: Submit the app for Google's standard verification (Standard Review).

steps.title: Initiate CASA Assessment
steps.detail: Engage an authorized lab for the CASA Tier 2 assessment and pay the required fee.

blockers.howToUnblock: Move app from 'Testing' to 'Production' status via verification to get long-lived tokens.

If you only need to send mail, request gmail.send (a sensitive scope: standard verification, no CASA) instead of mail.google.com. Reading mail needs a restricted scope (gmail.readonly, gmail.metadata, gmail.modify or mail.google.com), so plan for CASA in that case.

gotchas: Tokens expire after 7 days if the app status is set to Testing.
The 100-user limit in Testing mode is hard; new users cannot join once reached.
Authorized Domains list on the consent screen must include the redirect URI's domain.
Prompt=consent is recommended to ensure refresh tokens are always returned.

agentCanDo: Generate OAuth integration code for Web or CLI flows.
Draft the required Privacy Policy with 'Limited Use' clauses.
Outline the script for the YouTube verification demo video.
Research the minimum sufficient scopes for specific agent tasks.
youMustDo: Create and own the Google Cloud Project.
Record the YouTube demo video and upload it.
Pay the CASA assessment fees if restricted scopes are used.
Submit the final verification request in the Google Console.

claims.claim: CASA Tier 2 costs between $540 and $1,000 for automated self-serve track in 2026.
Refresh tokens in 'Testing' mode expire after 7 days.
OAuth discovery document is available and lists PKCE S256 support.
The mail.google.com scope is classified as a Restricted scope.
Standard verification takes 3-7 business days, while CASA takes 4-6 weeks.

openQuestions: Whether individual developers can qualify for even lower CASA fees than the $540 tier.
If the 100-user limit is enforced before or after the CASA assessment is required for External apps.
composioAdvice: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail, allowing you to bypass registration and verification during development. However, because Composio's default scopes include 'mail.google.com' (Restricted), you will eventually need your own app and a CASA assessment to scale. To delay this, if your agent only needs to send mail, use a custom OAuth app limited to 'gmail.send', which needs only standard verification. Any scope that reads mail (including 'gmail.readonly') is restricted and still requires CASA.

notes: Corrected: the agent suggested gmail.readonly might avoid the CASA assessment. Google lists gmail.readonly as a restricted scope (developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification); only send-only access (gmail.send) avoids CASA. Fixed in the blocker and in the Composio advice.
Confirmed against Google's docs: mail.google.com is restricted and triggers restricted-scope verification plus CASA; refresh tokens for apps in Testing status expire after 7 days.
Confirmed by probe: Google's discovery document advertises PKCE S256, and the authorize endpoint rejects an unknown client with 'Error 401: invalid_client'.
Not confirmed: the CASA price range ($540 to $1,000) comes from community and assessor sources; Google does not publish a fee.
